newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-YOUNG GIVES NZ ADVANTAGE VS SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YOUNG GIVES NZ ADVANTAGE VS SRI LANKA.

text.p: Opening batsman Bryan Young scored a test-best 154 not out on Friday to put New Zealand in a strong position at the close on the first day of the first cricket test against Sri Lanka at Carisbrook.
Young exacted a heavy toll on a disappointing Sri Lankan attack to earn his second test century as New Zealand enjoyed one of their better days in recent times to reach 343 for four by the close.
Rain stopped play briefly three overs before the scheduled close, but play resumed later to fill the daily quota of 90 overs.

On a pitch tailor-made for batsmen, Young, Matt Horne, who made a fluent 66, and skipper Stephen Fleming, who was at his best in compiling an elegant 51, made Sri Lankan captain Arjuna Ranatunga regret his decision to field first.
The tourists were clearly short of match play entering the test and it showed as their bowlers struggled to maintain a consistent line on a pitch demanding accuracy.
Young and his colleagues cashed in, with the Northern Districts batsman reaching three figures after tea when he drove a short delivery from offspinner Muttiah Muralitharan to the cover boundary.

Young's century took 272 minutes off 203 balls, 16 of which were boundaries. He has already surpassed his previous best test score of 120 and tomorrow the onus will rest on him to add further to an already healthy total.
He and Horne, playing in just his second test, put on 140 runs in 146 minutes to establish a New Zealand second-wicket record against Sri Lanka in an entertaining partnership.

Fleming, dropped on 40 by Pramodya Wickremasinghe at midoff, looked set for something special before perishing on 51 off just 59 deliveries. He attempted to hit seamer Wickremasinghe through midwicket but miscued the shot and offered Nuwan Zoysa an easy catch at mid-on.
Nathan Astle belted Wickremasinghe for 18 in one over and progressed to 27 before left-arm seamer Chaminda Vaas pierced his defences with the second new ball.

Left-arm fast bowler Zoysa, 18 and making his test debut, was the pick of the Sri Lankan bowlers, although he picked up no wickets, with his 23 overs costing 62 runs. Chaminda Vaas was the most successful bowler, picking up two for 81 from 21 overs.
